primary.title: The Jamaica Letter (Carta de Jamaica)
primary.author: Simón Bolívar
primary.rationale: A foundational document outlining Bolívar's vision for the future of Spanish America and his critique of Spanish rule. Widely translated and studied.

primary.title: Address to the Congress of Angostura (Discurso de Angostura)
primary.author: Simón Bolívar
primary.rationale: A pivotal speech delivered by Bolívar to the Congress of Angostura, proposing a new constitution for Venezuela and articulating his political philosophy.

primary.title: Memoirs of General Daniel F. E. von Bangemann
primary.author: Daniel F. E. von Bangemann
primary.rationale: While not authored by Bolívar, this work contains direct accounts and observations of Bolívar by a contemporary military officer who served with him. It offers valuable firsthand insights.

secondary.title: Simón Bolívar: A Self-Portrait
secondary.author: Simón Bolívar
secondary.rationale: A compilation of Bolívar's writings and speeches, offering direct insight into his thoughts and motivations. While compiled by others, it functions as a primary source collection.

secondary.title: Simón Bolívar: The Liberator
secondary.author: John Lynch
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive and highly regarded biography by a leading historian of Latin America, providing in-depth analysis of Bolívar's life, military campaigns, and political ideas.

secondary.title: The Cambridge History of Latin America, Volume 3: From Independence to c. 1930
secondary.author: Leslie Bethell (editor)
secondary.rationale: This volume contains scholarly chapters dedicated to the independence movements and the figures involved, including extensive analysis of Bolívar's role and impact.

suggestions.notes: Primary source selection prioritizes widely recognized and influential texts. Secondary sources are chosen for their scholarly reputation and recency. The inclusion of Bangemann's memoirs as a primary source is based on its direct observational content regarding Bolívar.
